findings.category: Cryptographic algorithm downgrade / key metadata mismatch
findings.explanation: The hardware identity key, which the wallet treats as its root of trust ('LoA High'), was limited to ES256. It now also accepts RS256. If the platform authenticator offers only RSA (some Windows Hello / TPM setups), it will create an RSA key. But the saved registration ignores the algorithm that was actually negotiated: it always records a hardcoded EC P-256 / ES256 JWK (with empty x/y). So the stored data claims ES256 while the device holds an RS256 key. The project's own algorithm list (crypto-agility.ts) marks RS256 as 'deprecated' and says to replace it with ES256, so this change lets a deprecated algorithm into the identity root of trust. Any verifier that relies on the stored alg label, or supports only ES256, will either fail or treat an unapproved key type as compliant.
findings.fix: Remove alg -257 from registerIdentityKey (keep ES256 only), or explicitly approve RS256 in the algorithm policy. In either case, read the real algorithm with response.getPublicKeyAlgorithm(), convert the SPKI from getPublicKey() into a real JWK instead of hardcoding EC/ES256, and reject at registration any algorithm the policy does not allow.
